page: Vultr vcg-a16-24c-256g-64vram is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for memory-intensive and parallel computing workloads. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical Intel x86_64 cores running at 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 16 MB L3 cache and supports AVX, AES, and FMA instructions. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB of RAM per core. Graphics acceleration is delivered by four NVIDIA Ampere A16 GPUs, providing a combined total of 64 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong capabilities in parallel processing and memory bandwidth. The system achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 41473.88 and a PassMark CPU score of 35340.23, placing both in the average tier. Large-block memory bandwidth tests recorded 137.58 GB/sec for read operations and 56.27 GB/sec for write operations. In LLM inference benchmarks, the server demonstrated top-tier performance for prompt processing, reaching 8464.24 tokens/sec with a small 135M model and 614.8 tokens/sec with a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds reached 253.1 tokens/sec for the 135M model and a strong 32.83 tokens/sec for the 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the combination of four dedicated GPUs, high memory capacity, and NVMe storage offers a balanced hardware profile for multi-tenant or highly parallelized workloads without requiring top-tier enterprise pricing. However, single-core performance remains average, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1766.38. This makes the instance less optimal for single-threaded tasks. The server is highly suited for workloads such as medium-scale LLM inference, parallel data processing, database operations, and GPU-accelerated rendering or virtualization tasks.
